old_caption: The video captures a close-up view of a wooden surface with several glass rods embedded in it. The rods are arranged in a row, and some of them have been shattered, creating a dramatic scene. The broken glass pieces are scattered around the rods, with some fragments still attached to the wood. The background is blurred, showing an outdoor setting with a clear blue sky and what appears to be a rocky hill or mountain range. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, focusing on the aftermath of the breakage. The lighting suggests it is daytime, with sunlight illuminating the scene. The overall atmosphere conveys a sense of sudden impact or force that caused the glass to shatter.

caption: The video captures a horizontal row of thin vertical glass panes mounted upright in a wooden beam, set against a blurred backdrop of reddish rock and pale blue sky. The panes on the left are already shattered, with jagged shards hanging suspended and a dense white dust cloud filling the gaps, while the right-side panes remain clear and intact. Tiny bright particles scatter through the air above the broken section. Throughout the excerpt the camera and background stay stationary, and no new break or collapse occurs. The white cloud slowly shifts shape and grows more diffuse at its edges, dispersing in place. The suspended shards remain essentially frozen, and the airborne specks drift and redistribute subtly. The overall state of destruction persists from the first frame to the last.

Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
